body:
m1 - a SECOND commit on the reference-scope tool, and it is a deliberate NON-change that I think matters more than the fix it follows. Head is now 7b13dfc on m1/resolution (770eb7b then 7b13dfc).

Having added `type` to the alternation, `opaque type` is the obvious next generalisation, and it is the one I would expect the next person to make. I went to make it. IT MAKES THE TOOL WORSE, and I only found that by measuring instead of reasoning.

WHAT I MEASURED. Every opaque type in core, story and features: AddressKey, AddressKind, BasisId, CanonicalId, Checksum, LanguageTag, MentionId, ModuleTag, PositiveInt, Probability, SidecarBlockRows, TokenIndex - and T. All of them except T have a companion object or class, so THE TOOL ALREADY FINDS THEM under that name. My worry was theoretical for twelve of thirteen.

The thirteenth is `opaque type T = String` at core/ids.scala:23 - an abstract type MEMBER of `abstract class OpaqueId`, not a standalone type. Adding `opaque` puts a bare `T` in the type list for any candidate touching ids.scala, and `grep -w T` matches 12 of 13 modules. The tool would name every module on every such change. That is not a wider safety margin; it is the loss of the signal, and it would land squarely on the core slice work in flight right now - slice 2 touches exactly these types.

So the alternation stays as it is, and the script now carries the measurement explaining why, so whoever notices the omission finds the answer rather than repeating the experiment.

I want to flag the shape of this, because it is the second time today the same move paid: I set out to close a gap I had already written down as a caveat, and the check turned the fix around. Earlier it was the ScoreEstimate caveat, which exposed a real bug in what I had sent you. This time it was the opaque caveat, which exposed that the fix would be harmful. The caveat is worth attacking precisely because it is where you have already admitted you do not know - and it cuts both ways, sometimes the gap is real and sometimes closing it costs more than leaving it.

VERIFICATION after both edits: 4383a85 still names codec, a9fd20f still names align/embed-bench/fixtures, ec0c439 still reports ScoreEstimate. No sbt gate - shell script, no Scala consumers, and reference-scope on the change names no modules.

Both commits are on bd-01M16R35WY3E82W83B86B6VTAK, still awaiting your gate on 770eb7b. Nothing else from me is pending; the signature stack landed and I am holding the remaining fields until you rule on the uniformCoverage non-migration argument and on whether distortedMass is mine or the engineer's.
